symptom: main went red immediately after ako/mxcli#1497 (the v1 BSON driver removal) merged: `mdl/backend/pagemutator/container_rendermode_test.go:8:2: no required module provides package go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson`, the package failing [setup failed], plus `--- FAIL: TestNoV1DriverImports ... imported again by 1 file(s)`
cause: Not a defect in either PR. ako/mxcli#1498 was authored and tested against a main that still required the v1 driver, and merged just before #1497 removed it. Neither PR conflicted with the other — different files — so nothing flagged the combination, and each was green on its own base. The file uses bson.D only, so the fix is the import path alone
insight: Removing a module the whole repo imports is not finished when the PR is green: any PR already open at that moment is still written against the old module, and a merge of two non-conflicting PRs can break main where neither breaks it alone. This happened TWICE in one change — first caught in-branch when merging origin/main pulled in #1495's 7 new v1 imports, then again post-merge from #1498 — so expect it rather than being surprised. TestNoV1DriverImports is what names the file both times, and its value is exactly here: a re-added import is not a build error while the module is still required, and after removal the compile error names only the package, not the reason. The structural fix is a repo setting, not code: require branches to be up to date before merging, for the window around any dependency removal. When it does happen, check the whole tree (`grep -rn '"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson'`) rather than only the file CI named — CI stops at the first [setup failed] package and a second offender would surface only on the next run
